# Run Vector Search ANN and ENN Queries

A MongoDB Vector Search query takes the form of an [aggregation pipeline](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/aggregation.md#std-label-aggregation) that uses [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) as the first stage. This page explains the syntax, options, and behavior of the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage.

The `$vectorSearch` stage performs a semantic search for a query vector on the specified field or fields. The field or fields must be indexed as the MongoDB Vector Search [vector](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector) type inside a [vectorSearch](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) type index.

**Note:**

MongoDB Vector Search supports ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search on Atlas Clusters running MongoDB v6.0.11, v7.0.2, or later and ENN (Exact Nearest Neighbor) search on Clusters running MongoDB v6.0.16, v7.0.10, v7.3.2, or later. You can also use MongoDB Vector Search with [self-managed](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/install-community.md#std-label-install-mdb-community-edition) or [local Atlas deployments](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/atlas-cli-deploy-local/) that you create with the Atlas CLI.

The `$vectorSearch` stage performs a semantic search for a query vector on the specified field or fields. The field or fields must be indexed as the MongoDB Vector Search [vector](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector) type inside a [vectorSearch](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) type index.

The `$vectorSearch` stage is used to perform a semantic search for a natural language query on the specified field. When using automated embeddings, the field or fields must be indexed as the MongoDB Vector Search [autoEmbed](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-auto-embed) type inside a [vectorSearch](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) type index.

**Important:**

Automated Embeddings is available as a Preview feature. The feature and the corresponding documentation might change at any time during the Preview period. Do not use this feature in your production environment. We do not use any customer data from this feature to train our models at this time. To learn more, see [Preview Features.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/preview-features/)

The `$vectorSearch` stage is used to perform a semantic search for a natural language query on the specified field. When using automated embeddings, the field or fields must be indexed as the MongoDB Vector Search [autoEmbed](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-auto-embed) type inside a [vectorSearch](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) type index.

## Supported Clients

You can run [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) queries by using the Atlas UI, MongoDB Compass, [`mongosh`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongosh), and any [MongoDB driver.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/)

You can also use MongoDB Vector Search with local Atlas deployments that you create with the Atlas CLI. To learn more, see [Create a Local Atlas Deployment.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/atlas-cli-deploy-local/)

[`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) is supported only on Atlas clusters running the following MongoDB versions:

- v6.0.11

- v7.0.2 and later (including RCs (Release Candidates)).

You can run [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) queries by using MongoDB Compass, [`mongosh`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongosh), and any [MongoDB driver.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/)

You can run [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) queries by using MongoDB Compass, [`mongosh`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongosh), and the following [MongoDB drivers:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/)

| MongoDB Driver | Version |
| --- | --- |
| [C#](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/) | 3.x or later |
| [Go](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/go/current/) | 2.x or later |
| [Java](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/java/sync/current/) | 5.x or later |
| [Node](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/) | 6.6.0 or later |
| [Python](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/python-drivers/) | 4.7 or later |
| [C++](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/cxx/) | 3.11.0 or later |
| [Rust](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/) | 3.1.0 or later |

## Syntax

The field that you want to search must be indexed as MongoDB Vector Search [vector](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector) type inside a [vectorSearch](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) index type.

A `$vectorSearch` pipeline has the following prototype form:

```javascript
{
  "$vectorSearch": {
    "exact": true | false,
    "index": "<index-name>",
    "limit": <number-of-results>,
    "numCandidates": <number-of-candidates>,
    "path": "<field-to-search>",
    "queryVector": [<array-of-numbers>],
    "filter": {<filter-specification>},
    "parentFilter": {<parent-filter-specification>}, 
    "nestedOptions": {
      "scoreMode": "max | avg"
    },
    "explainOptions": {
      "traceDocumentIds": [<array-of-documentIDs>]
    },
    "returnStoredSource": true | false,
    "searchNodePreference": {
      "key": <preference-string>
    }	   
  }
}

```

The field that you want to search must be indexed as MongoDB Vector Search [vector](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector) type inside a [vectorSearch](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) index type.

A `$vectorSearch` pipeline has the following prototype form:

```javascript
{
  "$vectorSearch": {
    "exact": true | false,
    "filter": {<filter-specification>},
    "index": "<index-name>",
    "limit": <number-of-results>,
    "numCandidates": <number-of-candidates>,
    "path": "<field-to-search>",
    "queryVector": [<array-of-numbers>],
    "explainOptions": {
      "traceDocumentIds": [<array-of-documentIDs>]
    },
    "parentFilter": {<parent-filter-specification>},
    "nestedOptions": {
      "scoreMode": "max | avg"
    },
    "returnStoredSource": true | false
  }
}
```

The field that you want to search must be indexed as MongoDB Vector Search [autoEmbed](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-auto-embed) type inside a [vectorSearch](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) index type.

A `$vectorSearch` pipeline has the following prototype form:

```javascript
{
  "$vectorSearch": {
    "exact": true | false,
    "filter": {<filter-specification>},
    "index": "<index-name>",
    "limit": <number-of-results>,
    "model": "<model-name>",
    "numCandidates": <number-of-candidates>,
    "path": "<field-to-search>",
    "query": {
      "text": "<query-text>"
    },
    "parentFilter": {<parent-filter-specification>}, 
    "nestedOptions": {
      "scoreMode": "max | avg"
    },
    "searchNodePreference": {
      "key": <preference-string>
    }      
  }
}

```

The field that you want to search must be indexed as MongoDB Vector Search [autoEmbed](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-auto-embed) type inside a [vectorSearch](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) index type.

A `$vectorSearch` pipeline has the following prototype form:

```javascript
{
  "$vectorSearch": {
    "exact": true | false,
    "filter": {<filter-specification>},
    "index": "<index-name>",
    "limit": <number-of-results>,
    "model": "<model-name>",
    "numCandidates": <number-of-candidates>,
    "path": "<field-to-search>",
    "query": {
      "text": "<query-text>"
    }
  }
}

```

## Fields

The `$vectorSearch` stage takes a document with the following fields:

| Field | Type | Necessity | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `exact` | Boolean | Optional | This is required if `numCandidates` is omitted. Flag that specifies whether to run ENN (Exact Nearest Neighbor) or ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search. Value can be one of the following: `false` - to run ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search; `true` - to run ENN (Exact Nearest Neighbor) search If omitted, defaults to `false`. MongoDB Vector Search supports ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search on Atlas Clusters running MongoDB v6.0.11, v7.0.2, or later and ENN (Exact Nearest Neighbor) search on Clusters running MongoDB v6.0.16, v7.0.10, v7.3.2, or later. You can also use MongoDB Vector Search with [self-managed](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/install-community.md#std-label-install-mdb-community-edition) or [local Atlas deployments](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/atlas-cli-deploy-local/) that you create with the Atlas CLI. To learn more about these search types, see [Vector Search Types.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline) |
| `explainOptions` | Object | Optional | Trace a list of vectors (identified by theirs `_id`) in an [explain](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/explain.md#std-label-avs-explain-ref) `executionStats` query. You can't use this option without `explain`. To learn more, see [Explain MongoDB Vector Search Results.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/explain.md#std-label-avs-explain-ref) |
| `explainOptions.``traceDocumentIds` | Array of objectIDs | Required | List of document `_id`s. |
| `filter` | Object | Optional | MQL (MongoDB Query Language) expression that uses an indexed field for pre-filtering the documents. You can filter on boolean, date, objectId, numeric, string, and UUID values, including arrays of these types. To learn which MQL operators MongoDB Vector Search supports in your filter, see [MongoDB Vector Search Filtering.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-filter) If you specify a `nestedRoot` in the index definition, the `filter` option applies to fields at the nested level. Use `parentFilter` to filter on root-level fields. If you specify both, MongoDB Vector Search combines them using `AND`. |
| `index` | String | Required | Name of the MongoDB Vector Search index to use. MongoDB Vector Search doesn't return results if you misspell the index name or if the specified index doesn't already exist on the cluster. |
| `limit` | Int | Required | Number (of type `int` only) of documents to return in the results. This value can't exceed the value of `numCandidates` if you specify `numCandidates`. |
| `nestedOptions` | Object | Optional | Configure how MongoDB Vector Search scores documents that contain nested arrays. |
| `nestedOptions.``scoreMode` | String | Optional | Specifies how to score documents that contain nested arrays. Value can be one of the following: `avg` - average the scores of the nested array elements.; `max` - use the maximum score of the nested array elements. |
| `numCandidates` | Int | Conditional | This field is required if `exact` is `false` or omitted. Number of nearest neighbors to use during the search. Value must be less than or equal to (`<=`) `10000`. You can't specify a number less than the number of documents to return (`limit`). We recommend that you specify a number at least 20 times higher than the number of documents to return (`limit`) to increase accuracy. This overrequest pattern is the recommended way to trade off latency and [recall](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-recall) in your ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) searches, and we recommend tuning this parameter based on your specific dataset size and query requirements. To learn more about other variables that might impact this parameter, see [`numCandidates` Selection.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-avs-num-candidates) |
| `parentFilter` | Object | Optional | MQL (MongoDB Query Language) expression that uses an indexed top-level field for pre-filtering the documents. You can filter on boolean, date, objectId, numeric, string, and UUID values, including arrays of these types. To learn which MQL operators MongoDB Vector Search supports in your filter, see [MongoDB Vector Search Filtering.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-filter) The `parentFilter` option is only valid if you specify a nested field (`nestedRoot`) in the index definition. If you specify the `parentFilter`, MongoDB Vector Search filters the top-level documents before filtering the nested documents. |
| `path` | String | Required | Indexed [vector](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector) type field to search. Use dot notation to specify path to embedded fields. You can query only one [vector](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector) type field per `$vectorSearch` stage. |
| `queryVector` | Array of Numbers | Required | Array of numbers of `float32`, BSON (Binary Javascript Object Notation) [BinData](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/BinData.md#std-label-server-binData-method) vectors with subtype `float32`, or BSON (Binary Javascript Object Notation) [BinData](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/BinData.md#std-label-server-binData-method) vectors with subtype `int1` or `int8` type that represent the query vector. To learn more about generating BSON (Binary Javascript Object Notation) `binData` vectors with subtype `float32`, `int8`, `int1`, see [How to Ingest Pre-Quantized Vectors.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md#std-label-avs-bindata-vector-subtype) The array size must match the number of vector `dimensions` specified in the [index definition](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) for the field. You must embed your query with the same model that you used to embed the data. You can query your embeddings with full-fidelity vectors, if the vector subtype is the same. This is only possible with `binData` vectors with subtype `float32`. If you use any other subtype (`int8` or `int1`), MongoDB Vector Search doesn't return any results or errors. |
| `returnStoredSource` | Boolean | Optional | Flag that specifies whether to perform a full document lookup on the backend database (`false`) or return only stored source fields directly from MongoDB Vector Search (`true`). If omitted, defaults to `false`. To learn more, see [Return Stored Source Fields.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-avs-return-stored-source) |
| `searchNodePreference` | Object | Optional | Document that enables preferential routing for this query. If you set a value for this field, Atlas executes this query against the same search node each time as long as that value remains the same, overriding the [default query routing](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/query-ref.md#std-label-about-mongot) behavior. This document contains a key-value pair where the value of `key` is an arbitrary string. IMPORTANT: Enabling this setting can improve the consistency of your search results, but doesn't guarantee perpetual consistency. Changes to your data set, index structure, cluster topology, or preferred node availability might still cause inconsistencies. |

You can also use MongoDB Vector Search with [self-managed](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/install-community.md#std-label-install-mdb-community-edition) or [local Atlas deployments](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/atlas-cli-deploy-local/) that you create with the Atlas CLI. To learn more about these search types, see [Vector Search Types.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline) |
| `filter` | Object | Optional | MQL (MongoDB Query Language) expression that compares an indexed field to use as a pre-filter. You can filter on boolean, date, objectId, numeric, string, and UUID values, including arrays of these types. To learn which MQL operators MongoDB Vector Search supports in your filter, see [MongoDB Vector Search Filtering.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-filter) |
| `index` | String | Required | Name of the MongoDB Vector Search index to use. MongoDB Vector Search doesn't return results if you misspell the index name or if the specified index doesn't already exist on the cluster. |
| `limit` | Int | Required | Number (of type `int` only) of documents to return in the results. This value can't exceed the value of `numCandidates` if you specify `numCandidates`. |
| `model` | String | Optional | Name of the embedding model to use for generating embeddings for the query string. The embedding model must be compatible with the embedding model specified in the index definition for the field against which you want to run the query. All the models in the `voyage-4` family of models are compatible with each other, but the `voyage-code-4` and `voyage-code-3` models are not compatible with any other model. Value can be one of the following: `voyage-4-large` - Highest-quality retrieval across languages and domains.; `voyage-4` - Balanced model for multilingual use and general-purpose retrieval accuracy. (Recommended); `voyage-4-lite` - Lightweight, faster model optimized for latency and lower cost.; `voyage-code-4` - Optimized for code retrieval. (Recommended for code) This embedding model is not compatible with any other supported embedding model. Therefore, you can't use this model if you indexed the field using a different embedding model.; `voyage-code-3` - Legacy model optimized for code retrieval. Use `voyage-code-4` instead. This embedding model is not compatible with any other supported embedding model. Therefore, you can't use this model if you indexed the field using a different embedding model. If omitted, defaults to the embedding model specified in the index definition. If you want to query using the `queryVector` parameter, you **must** omit this field. |
| `nestedOptions` | Object | Optional | Configure how MongoDB Vector Search scores documents that contain nested arrays. |
| `nestedOptions.``scoreMode` | String | Optional | Specifies how to score documents that contain nested arrays. Value can be one of the following: `avg` - average the scores of the nested array elements.; `max` - use the maximum score of the nested array elements. |
| `numCandidates` | Int | Conditional | This field is required if `exact` is `false` or omitted. Number of nearest neighbors to use during the search. Value must be less than or equal to (`<=`) `10000`. You can't specify a number less than the number of documents to return (`limit`). We recommend that you specify a number at least 20 times higher than the number of documents to return (`limit`) to increase accuracy. This overrequest pattern is the recommended way to trade off latency and [recall](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-recall) in your ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) searches, and we recommend tuning this parameter based on your specific dataset size and query requirements. To learn more about other variables that might impact this parameter, see [`numCandidates` Selection.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-avs-num-candidates) |
| `parentFilter` | Object | Optional | MQL (MongoDB Query Language) expression that uses an indexed top-level field for pre-filtering the documents. You can filter on boolean, date, objectId, numeric, string, and UUID values, including arrays of these types. To learn which MQL operators MongoDB Vector Search supports in your filter, see [MongoDB Vector Search Filtering.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-filter) The `parentFilter` option is only valid if you specify a nested field (`nestedRoot`) in the index definition. If you specify the `parentFilter`, MongoDB Vector Search filters the top-level documents before filtering the nested documents. |
| `path` | String | Required | Indexed [autoEmbed](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-auto-embed) type field to search. |
| `query` | Object | Optional | Object that specifies the query context. MongoDB Vector Search supports `text` query. This is mutually exclusive with `queryVector`. |
| `query.``text` | String | Required | Query text for which you want to perform the semantic search. MongoDB Vector Search automatically generates vector embeddings for the specified text using the `model` specified in the query or in the index definition. The embedding model specified in the query takes precedence. |
| `queryVector` | Array of Numbers | Optional | Array of vector embeddings or floating point numbers generated using a Voyage AI embedding model to perform a semantic search. To retrieve correct results, you must use a Voyage AI embedding model that is compatible with the Voyage AI embeddings model specified in the index definition for the field that you want to query. The format of the `queryVector` must match the `quantization` type configured in the index definition. If the formats don't match, MongoDB Vector Search returns empty results. Provide the `queryVector` in the following format for each `quantization` type: `scalar` - Provide a scalar-quantized vector. Because `scalar` is the default, provide a scalar-quantized vector when you omit the `quantization` field from the index definition.; `float` - Provide a float vector.; `binary` - Provide a float vector.; `binaryNoRescore` - Provide a binary-quantized vector. This is mutually exclusive with `model` and `query`. |
| `searchNodePreference` | Object | Optional | Document that enables preferential routing for this query. If you set a value for this field, Atlas executes this query against the same search node each time as long as that value remains the same, overriding the [default query routing](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/query-ref.md#std-label-about-mongot) behavior. This document contains a key-value pair where the value of `key` is an arbitrary string. IMPORTANT: Enabling this setting can improve the consistency of your search results, but doesn't guarantee perpetual consistency. Changes to your data set, index structure, cluster topology, or preferred node availability might still cause inconsistencies. |

## Vector Search Types

When you define a [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage, you can use the `exact` field to specify whether to run an ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) or ENN (Exact Nearest Neighbor) search.

### ANN Search

#### Approximate Nearest Neighbors (ANN) search

For Approximate Nearest Neighbors (ANN) search, MongoDB Vector Search finds vector embeddings in your data that are closest to the vector embedding in your query based on their proximity in multi-dimensional space and based on the number of neighbors that it considers. It uses the [Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.09320) algorithm and finds the vector embeddings most similar to the vector embedding in your query without scanning every vector. Therefore, ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search is ideal for querying large datasets without significant filtering.

**Note:**

Optimal [recall](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-recall) for ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search is typically considered to be around 90-95% overlap in results with ENN (Exact Nearest Neighbor) search but with significantly lower latency. This provides a good balance between accuracy and performance. To achieve this with MongoDB Vector Search, [tune](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-avs-num-candidates) the `numCandidates` parameter at query time.

#### `numCandidates` Selection

You must specify the `numCandidates` field to run ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search. This field determines how many nearest neighbors MongoDB Vector Search considers during the search.

When you perform a vector search using the [Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.09320) index structure, MongoDB Vector Search accumulates results by populating a priority queue. The `numCandidates` parameter controls the size of this queue, which determines how long to search before returning the top `limit` results. A larger queue (higher `numCandidates`) allows the search to explore more of the [Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.09320) graph, potentially finding better matches at the cost of increased query latency.

We recommend that you specify a `numCandidates` number at least 20 times higher than the number of documents to return (`limit`) to increase accuracy and reduce discrepancies between your ENN (Exact Nearest Neighbor) and ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) query results. For example, if you set `limit` to return `5` results, consider setting `numCandidates` to `100` as a starting point. To learn more, see [How to Measure the Accuracy of Your Query Results.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md#std-label-avs-improve-results)

This overrequest pattern is the recommended way to trade off latency and [recall](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-recall) in your ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) searches. However, we recommend tuning the `numCandidates` parameter based on your specific dataset size and query requirements. To ensure that you get accurate results, consider the following variables:

- **Index Size**: Larger collections typically require higher `numCandidates` values to maintain recall. A collection with millions of vectors might need significantly more candidates than one with thousands of vectors.

- **Limit Value**: Because `numCandidates` is highly correlated with the index size, low `limit` values require proportionally higher `numCandidates` values to maintain recall.

- **Vector Quantization**: [Quantized vectors](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-quantization) reduce storage at the cost of accuracy. Using quantized vectors (`int8` or `int1` subtypes) might require higher `numCandidates` values compared to full precision `float32` vectors to maintain similar recall.

* **Index Size**: Larger collections typically require higher `numCandidates` values to maintain recall. A collection with millions of vectors might need significantly more candidates than one with thousands of vectors.

* **Limit Value**: Because `numCandidates` is highly correlated with the index size, low `limit` values require proportionally higher `numCandidates` values to maintain recall.

### ENN Search

#### Exact Nearest Neighbors (ENN) search

For an Exact Nearest Neighbors (ENN) search, MongoDB Vector Search exhaustively searches all the indexed vector embeddings by calculating the distance between all the embeddings and finds the exact nearest neighbor for the vector embedding in your query. This is computationally intensive and might negatively impact query latency. Therefore, we recommend ENN (Exact Nearest Neighbor) searches for the following use-cases:

- You want to determine the [recall](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-recall) and accuracy of your ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) query using the ideal, exact results for the ENN (Exact Nearest Neighbor) query.

- You want to query less than 10000 documents without having to tune the number of nearest neighbors to consider.

- Your want to include selective pre-filters in your query against collections where less than 5% of your data meets the given pre-filter.

If you enable automatic quantization, MongoDB Vector Search uses only the full-fidelity vectors for ENN (Exact Nearest Neighbor) queries.

- You want to determine the [recall](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-recall) and accuracy of your ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) query using the ideal, exact results for the ENN (Exact Nearest Neighbor) query.

- You want to query less than 10000 documents without having to tune the number of nearest neighbors to consider.

- Your want to include selective pre-filters in your query against collections where less than 5% of your data meets the given pre-filter.

## Considerations

[`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) must be the first stage of any pipeline where it appears.

### Best Practices

Automated Embedding imposes rate limits on the number of requests you can make and the number of tokens you can use within a specific time frame. This is measured in tokens per minute (TPM) and requests per minute (RPM) to ensure fair usage, prevent abuse, and maintain the stability and performance of the endpoint service for all users. To learn more, see [Rate Limits](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/crud-embeddings/automated-embedding/models.md#std-label-auto-embed-rate-limits). You can request for a rate limit increase by [contacting support.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/support.md#std-label-request-support)

You can use a different model in your query, which is compatible with the model used to create the index. This allows you to have different price and retrieval quality tradeoffs for your queries. For example, you can use a smaller model for queries to reduce the cost while having a larger model during indexing to improve the retrieval accuracy. To learn more, see [Compatible Model Query example.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-egs)

### Query Cancellation

You can use the [`cursor.maxTimeMS()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.maxTimeMS.md#mongodb-method-cursor.maxTimeMS) cursor option to specify a cumulative time limit (in milliseconds) for processing a [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) query. If you specify the `maxTimeMS` option with your query and the time limit expires, MongoDB Vector Search terminates the query and returns an error.

For many queries, most of the latency occurs after `mongot` returns results, while `mongod` looks up the full documents that match the returned IDs. To effectively reduce resource usage, set the time limit expiration to cancel the query while `mongot` is still running.

**Note:**

Starting in MongoDB v8.3, if the time limit expires while `mongot` is still running the Lucene search, `mongot` also stops that search, which reduces resource usage on the `mongot` process. On earlier versions, `mongod` still cancels the query and returns the same error, but `mongot` continues running the Lucene search to completion.

```shell
db.embedded_movies.aggregate([
  {
    "$vectorSearch": {
      ...
    }
  }
]).maxTimeMS(120)
```

**Output:**

```json
MongoServerError[MaxTimeMSExpired]: Executor error during aggregate command on namespace: sample_mflix.embedded_movies :: caused by :: operation exceeded time limit
```

The preceding example uses the `maxTimeMS` option to cancel a query against the `sample_mflix.embedded_movies` collection after 120 milliseconds.

### Best Practices

Voyage AI imposes rate limits on the number of requests you can make within a specific time frame, often measured in tokens per minute (TPM) or requests per minute (RPM) to ensure fair usage, prevent abuse, and maintain the stability and performance of the endpoint service for all users. Rate limits follow a tiered system. To learn more about the different tiers for keys you created from:

- Atlas UI, see [Usage Tiers](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/voyageai/management/rate-limits.md#std-label-voyage-rate-limits)

- Voyage AI, see [Rate Limits](https://docs.voyageai.com/docs/rate-limits/)

If you exceed the number of requests or tokens in the most recent minute, the endpoint service denies any subsequent additional request and returns a `429` (Rate Limit Exceeded) HTTP (HyperText Transport Protocol) status code. We recommend the following if you hit the rate limit:

- Insert a wait period between each request.

- Backoff and wait for an exponentially increased time before trying again. Wait until the request is successful or until you reach a maximum number of retries.

You can use a different model in your query, which is compatible with the model used to create the index. This allows you to have different price and retrieval quality tradeoffs for your queries. For example, you can use a smaller model for queries to reduce the cost while having a larger model during indexing to improve the retrieval accuracy. To learn more, see [Compatible Model Query example.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-egs)

### Limitations

[`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) can't be used in [view definition](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/views.md#std-label-views-landing-page) and the following pipeline stages:

- [`$lookup`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/lookup.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-lookup) sub-pipeline&#x20;

- [`$facet`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/facet.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-facet) pipeline stage

You can pass the results of [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) to this stage.

### MongoDB Vector Search Indexing

You must index the fields to search using the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage inside a [vectorSearch](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) type index definition. You can index the following types of fields in a MongoDB Vector Search [vectorSearch](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) type index definition:

- Fields that contain vector embeddings as [vector](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) type.

- Additional fields as the [filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) type to enable vector search on pre-filtered data.

You must index the fields to search using the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage inside a [vectorSearch](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) type index definition. You can index the following types of fields in a MongoDB Vector Search [vectorSearch](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) type index definition:

- Fields that contain text as [autoEmbed](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-auto-embed) type.

- Additional fields as the [filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) type to enable vector search on pre-filtered data.

To learn more about these MongoDB Vector Search field types, see [How to Index Fields for Vector Search.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search)

### MongoDB Vector Search Scoring

MongoDB Vector Search assigns a score, in a fixed range from `0` to `1` (where `0` indicates low similarity and `1` indicates high similarity), to every document that it returns.

The score is calculated according to the `similarity` function that you specify in the MongoDB Vector Search [index definition](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search-options). To learn more about the `similarity` options you can choose from, see [About the Similarity Functions.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-similarity-functions)

#### `vectorSearchScore`

Each returned document includes the score as metadata. To return each document's score along with the result set, use a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage in your aggregation pipeline and configure the `score` as a field to project. In the `score` field, specify a [`$meta`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/meta.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-meta) expression with the value `vectorSearchScore`. The syntax is as follows:

```javascript
db.<collection>.aggregate([
{
   "$vectorSearch": {
      <query-syntax>
   }
},
{
   "$project": {
      "<field-to-include>": 1,
      "<field-to-exclude>": 0,
      "score": { "$meta": "vectorSearchScore" }
   }
}
])
```

**Note:**

You can use `vectorSearchScore` as a `score` [`$meta`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/meta.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-meta) expression only after the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) pipeline stage. If you use `vectorSearchScore` after any other query, MongoDB logs a warning starting in MongoDB v8.2.

#### `nestedOptions`

Use `nestedOptions` if you are querying a MongoDB Vector Search index that has `nestedRoot` specified in the index definition.

The `nestedOptions` field controls how the individual scores from multiple matching vector embeddings from child documents are combined to calculate a single relevance score for the overall parent document that is returned in the results.

If you omit this field, the `scoreMode` defaults to `max`.

`max`

When `scoreMode` is set to `max`, MongoDB Vector Search uses the maximum score from the matching child documents as the overall score for the parent document. Use this if you want the parent document to be ranked based on its single most relevant nested item.

`avg`

When `scoreMode` is set to `avg`, MongoDB Vector Search calculates the average score of all the matching child documents as the overall score for the parent document. Use this if you want the parent document to be ranked based on the relevance of all of its nested items.

The score is calculated according to the `similarity` function that you specify in the MongoDB Vector Search [index definition](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search-options). To learn more about the `similarity` options you can choose from, see [About the Similarity Functions.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-similarity-functions)

Each returned document includes the score as metadata. To return each document's score along with the result set, use a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage in your aggregation pipeline and configure the `score` as a field to project. In the `score` field, specify a [`$meta`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/meta.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-meta) expression with the value `vectorSearchScore`. The syntax is as follows:

```javascript
db.<collection>.aggregate([
   {
      "$vectorSearch": {
         <query-syntax>
      }
   },
   {
      "$project": {
         "<field-to-include>": 1,
         "<field-to-exclude>": 0,
         "score": { "$meta": "vectorSearchScore" }
      }
   }
])
```

The score is calculated according to the `similarity` function that you specify in the MongoDB Vector Search [index definition](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search-options). To learn more about the `similarity` options you can choose from, see [About the Similarity Functions.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-similarity-functions)

Each returned document includes the score as metadata. To return each document's score along with the result set, use a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage in your aggregation pipeline and configure the `score` as a field to project. In the `score` field, specify a [`$meta`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/meta.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-meta) expression with the value `vectorSearchScore`. The syntax is as follows:

```javascript
db.<collection>.aggregate([
   {
      "$vectorSearch": {
         <query-syntax>
      }
   },
   {
      "$project": {
         "<field-to-include>": 1,
         "<field-to-exclude>": 0,
         "score": { "$meta": "vectorSearchScore" }
      }
   }
])
```

**Note:**

You can use `vectorSearchScore` as a `score` [`$meta`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/meta.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-meta) expression only after the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) pipeline stage. If you use `vectorSearchScore` after any other query, MongoDB logs a warning starting in MongoDB v8.2.

**Note:**

Pre-filtering your data doesn't affect the score that MongoDB Vector Search returns using `vectorSearchScore` for [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) queries.

### MongoDB Vector Search Filtering

MongoDB Vector Search supports data filtering. You can:

- [Pre-filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vector-search-pre-filter) your data by using the `filter` option in your MongoDB Vector Search query.

- [post-filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vector-search-post-filter) the results of your MongoDB Vector Search query by using [`$match`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/match.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-match) and other supported [aggregation pipeline stages.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline.md#std-label-aggregation-pipeline)

![Atlas Vector Search Pre-Filter and Post-Filter](/images/pipeline/avs-pre-post-filter.png)

MongoDB Vector Search performs pre-filter and post-filter operations independently on segments of data. The HNSW graph for each segment is based on only the vectors in that segment. MongoDB Vector Search applies the filters to each segment's documents to eliminate documents that don't meet the filter criteria. Pre-filtering ensures that documents are eliminated before MongoDB Vector Search traverses the HNSW graph and post-filtering ensures that irrelevant documents or fields in the documents are eliminated from the vector search results.

#### Pre-Filter Search Data

You can pre-filter your data to narrow the scope of your semantic search and ensure that only relevant vectors are considered for comparison. When you pre-filter your data by using the `filter` option, MongoDB Vector Search performs the semantic search on only a subset of your data, which increases the accuracy of your search results.

Pre-filtering can be too restrictive, as the pre-filter may exclude data that doesn't exactly match the pre-filter, but is semantically similar to the query you want to consider during the vector search. To mitigate this, we recommend setting a broad filter criteria to ensure your query does the following:

- Includes as many relevant results as possible.

- Excludes irrelevant data from the results.

- Returns the requested number of documents in the results.

**Important:**

Filtered queries are typically slower than an otherwise equivalent unfiltered query.

##### Pre-Filter for Top-Level Embeddings

The [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) `filter` option matches BSON (Binary Javascript Object Notation) boolean, date, objectId, numeric, string, and UUID values, including arrays of these types.

You **must** index the fields that you want to filter your data by as the [filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) type in a [vectorSearch](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) type index definition. Filtering your data is useful to narrow the scope of your semantic search and ensure that not all vectors are considered for comparison.

MongoDB Vector Search supports the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) `filter` option for the following MQL (MongoDB Query Language) [operators:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/query-operators/)

| Type | MQL (MongoDB Query Language) operator |
| --- | --- |
| Equality | [`$eq`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/eq.md#mongodb-query-op.-eq), [`$ne`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/ne.md#mongodb-query-op.-ne) |
| Range | [`$gt`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/gt.md#mongodb-query-op.-gt), [`$lt`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/lt.md#mongodb-query-op.-lt), [`$gte`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/gte.md#mongodb-query-op.-gte), [`$lte`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/lte.md#mongodb-query-op.-lte) |
| In set | [`$in`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/in.md#mongodb-query-op.-in), [`$nin`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/nin.md#mongodb-query-op.-nin) |
| Existence | [`$exists`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists.md#mongodb-query-op.-exists) |
| Logical | [`$not`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/not.md#mongodb-query-op.-not), [`$nor`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/nor.md#mongodb-query-op.-nor), [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/and.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-and), [`$or`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/or.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-or) |

**Note:**

The [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) `filter` option doesn't support other [query operators](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/query-predicates.md#std-label-query-predicates-ref), [aggregation pipeline operators](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions), or [MongoDB Search operators.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/operators-collectors/overview.md#std-label-operators-ref)

##### Pre-Filter for Nested Embeddings

For nested embeddings, the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) supports the `filter` and `parentFilter` options to pre-filter the data. Use the:

- `filter` option to filter by child or nested embedded document fields of the field specified as the `nestedRoot` in the index definition.

- `parentFilter` to filter by root-level fields.

You can't combine the `filter` and `parentFilter` options using `OR`. When you specify both, MongoDB Vector Search implicitly combines both using `AND` and both *must* match.

The [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) `filter` option matches BSON (Binary Javascript Object Notation) boolean, date, objectId, numeric, string, and UUID values, including arrays of these types.

You **must** index the fields that you want to filter your data by as the [filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) type in a [vectorSearch](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) type index definition. Filtering your data is useful to narrow the scope of your semantic search and ensure that not all vectors are considered for comparison.

MongoDB Vector Search supports the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) `filter` option for the following MQL (MongoDB Query Language) [operators:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/query-operators/)

| Type | MQL (MongoDB Query Language) operator |
| --- | --- |
| Equality | [`$eq`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/eq.md#mongodb-query-op.-eq), [`$ne`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/ne.md#mongodb-query-op.-ne) |
| Range | [`$gt`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/gt.md#mongodb-query-op.-gt), [`$lt`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/lt.md#mongodb-query-op.-lt), [`$gte`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/gte.md#mongodb-query-op.-gte), [`$lte`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/lte.md#mongodb-query-op.-lte) |
| In set | [`$in`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/in.md#mongodb-query-op.-in), [`$nin`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/nin.md#mongodb-query-op.-nin) |
| Existence | [`$exists`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists.md#mongodb-query-op.-exists) |
| Logical | [`$not`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/not.md#mongodb-query-op.-not), [`$nor`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/nor.md#mongodb-query-op.-nor), [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/and.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-and), [`$or`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/or.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-or) |

**Note:**

The [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) `filter` option doesn't support other [query operators](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/query-predicates.md#std-label-query-predicates-ref), [aggregation pipeline operators](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions), or [MongoDB Search operators.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/operators-collectors/overview.md#std-label-operators-ref)

#### Post-Filter Search Results

If your index size isn't optimal for pre-filtering or if you set broad pre-filtering criteria, you can post-filter your vector search results to return only relevant data. To filter the results of your vector search, you can use any supported [aggregation pipeline stage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline.md#std-label-aggregation-pipeline), such as the [`$match`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/match.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-match) stage, after the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage. To learn more, see [Additional Performance Recommendations.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/benchmark/performance-recommendations.md#std-label-avs-performance-recommendations)

To select the fields to return in the results, use the [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage unless you need all the fields in the results. We recommend excluding the vector field in the [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to improve query performance.

For example, you can use the [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to include the `vectorSearchScore` and then use the [`$match`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/match.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-match) stage to return only documents above a certain score threshold.

#### Filtering Considerations

- MongoDB Vector Search supports the short form of [`$eq`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/eq.md#mongodb-query-op.-eq). In the short form, you don't need to specify `$eq` in the query.

  For example, consider the following filter with `$eq`:

  ```json
  "filter": { "_id": { "$eq": ObjectId("5a9427648b0beebeb69537a5") }
  ```

  This is equivalent to the following filter, which uses the short form of `$eq`:

  ```json
  "filter": { "_id": ObjectId("5a9427648b0beebeb69537a5") }
  ```

- You can use the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/and.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-and) MQL (MongoDB Query Language) operator to specify an array of filters in a single query.

  For example, consider the following pre-filter for documents with a `genres` field equal to `Action` and a `year` field with the value `1999`, `2000`, or `2001`:

  ```json
  "filter": {
    "$and": [
      { "genres": "Action" },
      { "year": { "$in": [ 1999, 2000, 2001 ] } }
    ]
  }
  ```

- For advanced filtering capabilities such as fuzzy search, phrase matching, location filtering, and other analyzed text, use the [vectorSearch](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/operators-collectors/vectorSearch.md#std-label-fts-vectorSearch-ref) operator in a [`$search`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/aggregation-stages/search.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-search) stage.

##### Return Stored Source Fields

If you configured the [storedSource](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-stored-source-definition) option in the [index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-types-vector-search) for a collection, MongoDB Vector Search stores the specified fields on `mongot`. You can use the `returnStoredSource` boolean option in your MongoDB Vector Search queries to retrieve only those fields, rather than fetching full documents from the collection.

By default, MongoDB Vector Search performs full document lookup implicitly on the backend database after MongoDB Vector Search matches documents for the query. This lookup could significantly degrade performance for subsequent aggregation pipeline stages that fetch all matched dataset from [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage.

If you configured the `storedSource` option, you can use the `returnStoredSource` option to retrieve only parts of the documents directly stored on MongoDB Vector Search and avoid full document lookup on the database. This allows you to perform most database-side filtering operations on documents with a minimum number of fields. You can then retrieve all the fields from the documents at a later stage in the pipeline using [`$lookup`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/lookup.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-lookup)

###### Behavior

You can set one of the following values for the  `returnStoredSource` option:

- `true` - to return only stored source fields directly from MongoDB Vector Search

- `false` - to do an implicit full document lookup on the backend database (default)

If you run MongoDB Vector Search queries with the `returnStoredSource` boolean option set to `true`:

- MongoDB Vector Search returns an empty document if the document doesn't include the fields configured for storing.

- MongoDB Vector Search returns errors if the index definition doesn't include the Stored Source configuration.

- MongoDB Vector Search might return stale data due to a replication lag.

- MongoDB Vector Search might return duplicate data on sharded clusters.

If you perform a high volume and rate of data insert and update operations for your collection on the backend database, MongoDB Vector Search might return stale data because the data stored on `mongot` might not be current due to a replication lag. You can view the approximate number of milliseconds that MongoDB Vector Search is behind in replicating changes from the [oplog](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-oplog) of [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) in the Atlas UI. To learn more, see [Review MongoDB Search Metrics.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/review-atlas-search-metrics.md#std-label-review-atlas-search-metrics)

If there are [orphaned documents](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-orphaned-document) during chunk migration, MongoDB Vector Search might return duplicate documents for queries against sharded cluster.

###### Sample Use

If many of the results of the `$vectorSearch` stage are discarded afterward and you need to perform implicit document lookup on your database, we recommend using the `returnStoredSource` option. You can store fields required for sorting or filtering and use `returnStoredSource` option at query time to perform the following actions:

1. Intermediate operations on partial documents returned by MongoDB Vector Search.

2. [`$lookup`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/lookup.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-lookup) at the end of the pipeline if full documents are needed.

**Important:**

For efficiency, configure only a minimum number of fields for storage on MongoDB Vector Search. Use this option if your documents are large enough to cause issues during lookup.

##### Parallel Query Execution Across Segments

We recommend dedicated [Search Nodes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-config/multi-cloud-distribution.md#std-label-configure-search-nodes) to isolate vector search query processing. You might see improved query performance on the dedicated Search Nodes. Note that the high-CPU systems might provide more performance improvement. When MongoDB Vector Search runs on search nodes, MongoDB Vector Search parallelizes query execution across segments of data.

Parallelization of query processing improves the response time in many cases, such as queries on large datasets. Using intra-query parallelism during MongoDB Vector Search query processing utilizes more resources, but improves latency for each individual query.

**Note:**

MongoDB Vector Search doesn't guarantee that each query will run concurrently. For example, when too many concurrent queries are queued, MongoDB Vector Search might fall back to single-threaded execution.

You might see inconsistent results for the same successive queries. To mitigate this, increase the value of `numCandidates` in your [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) queries.

## Examples

The following queries search the [sample dataset](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/import/load-sample-data.md#std-label-load-sample-data) using the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage. If you load the sample data and create the MongoDB Vector Search indexes for the collections, you can run the sample [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) queries against these collections.

The following queries search the [sample dataset](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sample-data.md#std-label-atlas-sample-data) using the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage. The queries search the field indexed as the `autoEmbed` type, for which MongoDB Vector Search automatically generates embeddings using the `model` specified in the index definition.

When you run a text query against the indexed `autoEmbed` type field, MongoDB Vector Search automatically generates embeddings for the text string in your query using the embedding model that you specified in the query or the the index used by the query. It uses the embeddings to search the index for documents that are semantically similar to the specified query text.

### Prerequisites

Before you run these examples, perform the following actions:

- Add the [sample dataset](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/import/load-sample-data.md#std-label-load-sample-data) used in the query to your cluster.

- Create MongoDB Vector Search indexes for the collection. For instructions, see the [Create a MongoDB Vector Search Index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-create-index) procedure and configure the index for the sample queries in your desired language.

### Queries

**Note:**

Pasting the `queryVector` from the sample code into your terminal might take a while depending on your machine.

#### Simple Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *time travel*. It considers up to `150` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot` and `title` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the [vector search score](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-score) for each document in the results.

2. Load the file into [`mongosh`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongosh) to use the embeddings in your query:

   ```javascript
   load('/<path-to-file>/query-embeddings.js');
   ```

3. Run the following query:

   ```json
   db.embedded_movies.aggregate([
     {
       "$vectorSearch": {
         "index": "vector_index",
         "path": "plot_embedding_voyage_3_large",
         "queryVector": TIME_TRAVEL_EMBEDDING,
         "numCandidates": 150,
         "limit": 10,
         "quantization": "scalar"
       }
     },
     {
       "$project": {
         "_id": 0,
         "plot": 1,
         "title": 1,
         "score": { $meta: "vectorSearchScore" }
       }
     }
   ])
   ```

#### Filter Query

The following query filters the documents for movies released between January 01, `1955` and January 01, `1975` before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `150` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *kids adventure*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

MongoDB Vector Search filters the documents based on the `year` field value that ranges between 1955 and 1975. It returns documents that summarize children's adventures in the plot for movies released between 1955 and 1975.

**See also: Additional Filter Examples**

The [MongoDB Vector Search Quick Start Tutorial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/tutorials/quick-start.md#std-label-vector-search-quick-start) tutorial demonstrates other pre-filters in semantic search queries against the embedded data in the `sample_mflix.embedded_movies` collection.

#### Return Stored Source Query

The following query uses the `returnStoredSource` option to `true` to return only the [stored source fields](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-stored-source-definition) directly from MongoDB Vector Search, avoiding a full document lookup on the backend database. The query filters the documents for movies released between `1970` and `2020`, both inclusive, before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `1000` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *martial arts*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and return only the fields stored on `mongot`.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

#### Nested Field Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `reviews.comments_embedding` field in the `sample_airbnb.listingsAndReviews` collection using vector embeddings for the string *great location close to everything*. It considers up to `100` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results.

The query pre-filters the documents by matching the `address.country` field value to *United States* and number of bedrooms between 2 and 3. It then uses the `nestedOptions` option to return the document that has the *average* score from the matching child documents as the overall score for the parent document.

The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `name`, `address`, and `reviews.comments` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

Create the embeddings for the nested field and index the collection by following the instructions in [Procedure.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-create-index-procedure)

2. Load the file into [`mongosh`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongosh) to use the embeddings in your query:

   ```javascript
   load('/<path-to-file>/query-embeddings.js');
   ```

3. Run the query:

   ```json
   db.listingsAndReviews.aggregate([
     {
       "$vectorSearch": {
         "index": "vector_index",
         "filter": {
           "reviews.date": { "$gte": ISODate("2010-01-01") }
         },
         "parentFilter": {
           "address.country": { "$in": ["United States"] },
           "bedrooms": { "$gte": 2,  "$lte": 3 }, 
           "property_type": { "$in": ["Apartment", "House"] }
         },
         "path": "reviews.comments_embedding",
         "queryVector": GREAT_LOCATION_EMBEDDING,
         "numCandidates": 100,
         "limit": 5,
         "nestedOptions": {
           "scoreMode": "avg"
         }
       }
     },
     {
       "$project": {
         "_id": 0,
         "name": 1,
         "address": 1,
         "neighborhood_overview": 1,
         "bedrooms": 1,
         "property_type": 1,
         "reviews.comments": 1,
         "score": { "$meta": "vectorSearchScore" }
       }
     }
   ])
   ```

2. Load the file into [`mongosh`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongosh) to use the embeddings in your query.

   ```javascript
   load('/<path-to-file>/query-embeddings.js');
   ```

3. Run the query.

   ```shell
   db.embedded_movies.aggregate([
     {
       "$vectorSearch": {
         "index": "vector_index",
         "path": "plot_embedding_voyage_3_large",
         "queryVector": WORLD_WAR_EMBEDDING,
         "exact": true,
         "limit": 10
       }
     },
     {
       "$project": {
         "_id": 0,
         "plot": 1,
         "title": 1,
         "score": { $meta: "vectorSearchScore" }
       }
     }
   ])
   ```

#### Simple Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `fullplot` field. The query automatically generates vector embeddings for the string *young heroes caught in epic struggles
between light and darkness* using the same model that was used in the index to perform a semantic search. It considers up to `100` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `fullplot` and `title` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the [vector search score](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-score) for each document in the results.

```cpp
#include <bsoncxx/builder/basic/document.hpp>
#include <bsoncxx/json.hpp>
#include <iostream>
#include <mongocxx/client.hpp>
#include <mongocxx/instance.hpp>
#include <mongocxx/pipeline.hpp>
#include <mongocxx/uri.hpp>

using bsoncxx::builder::basic::kvp;
using bsoncxx::builder::basic::make_document;

int main() {
  mongocxx::instance inst;

  // Replace the placeholder with your Atlas connection string
  const auto uri = mongocxx::uri{"<connection-string>"};

  // Connect to your cluster
  auto client = mongocxx::client{uri};
  auto collection = client["sample_mflix"]["movies"];

  // Define the pipeline with vectorSearch query options
  mongocxx::pipeline stages;

  stages
      .append_stage(make_document(kvp(
          "$vectorSearch",
          make_document(
              kvp("index", "autoembed_index"), kvp("path", "fullplot"),
              kvp("query",
                  make_document(kvp("text",
                                    "young heroes caught in epic struggles "
                                    "between light and darkness"))),
              kvp("numCandidates", 100), kvp("limit", 10)))))
      .project(make_document(
          kvp("_id", 0), kvp("title", 1), kvp("fullplot", 1),
          kvp("score", make_document(kvp("$meta", "vectorSearchScore")))));

  // Run the query and print the results
  auto cursor = collection.aggregate(stages);

  for (auto&& doc : cursor) {
    std::cout << bsoncxx::to_json(doc) << std::endl;
  }

  return 0;
}

```

#### Compatible Model Query

The following example uses the `voyage-4-large` model to query the index that was built using the `voyage-4` model. The query automatically generates vector embeddings for the string *young heroes caught in epic struggles between
light and darkness* using the `voyage-4-large` embedding model, which is compatible with the `voyage-4` model used to index the `fullplot` field. The query specifies the following criteria to pre-filter the documents for the semantic search:

- Include only movies released between the years `1980` to `2020`, both inclusive.

- Include only movies in the genres `Action`, `Adventure`, and `Family`.

```cpp
#include <bsoncxx/builder/basic/document.hpp>
#include <bsoncxx/json.hpp>
#include <iostream>
#include <mongocxx/client.hpp>
#include <mongocxx/instance.hpp>
#include <mongocxx/pipeline.hpp>
#include <mongocxx/uri.hpp>

using bsoncxx::builder::basic::kvp;
using bsoncxx::builder::basic::make_document;

int main() {
  mongocxx::instance inst;

  // Replace the placeholder with your Atlas connection string
  const auto uri = mongocxx::uri{"<connection-string>"};

  // Connect to your cluster
  auto client = mongocxx::client{uri};
  auto collection = client["sample_mflix"]["movies"];

  // Define the pipeline with vectorSearch query options
  mongocxx::pipeline stages;

  stages
      .append_stage(make_document(kvp(
          "$vectorSearch",
          make_document(
              kvp("index", "autoembed_index"), kvp("path", "fullplot"),
              kvp("query",
                  make_document(kvp("text",
                                    "young heroes caught in epic struggles "
                                    "between light and darkness"))),
              kvp("model", "voyage-4-large"), kvp("numCandidates", 100),
              kvp("limit", 10)))))
      .project(make_document(
          kvp("_id", 0), kvp("title", 1), kvp("fullplot", 1), kvp("year", 1),
          kvp("genres", 1),
          kvp("score", make_document(kvp("$meta", "vectorSearchScore")))));

  // Run the query and print the results
  auto cursor = collection.aggregate(stages);

  for (auto&& doc : cursor) {
    std::cout << bsoncxx::to_json(doc) << std::endl;
  }

  return 0;
}

```
