#### Filter Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `fullplot` field for movies. The query automatically generates vector embeddings for the string *epic fantasy journey with reluctant
heroes* using the `voyage-4` embedding model, which is the model specified in the index for the `fullplot` field, to perform a semantic search. The query specifies the following criteria to pre-filter the documents for the semantic search:

- Include only movies released between the years `1980` to `2020`, both inclusive.

- Include only movies in the genres `Action`, `Adventure`, and `Family`.

It considers up to `100` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `fullplot`, `genres`, and `title` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the [vector search score](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-score) for each document in the results.

```cpp
#include <bsoncxx/builder/basic/array.hpp>
#include <bsoncxx/builder/basic/document.hpp>
#include <bsoncxx/json.hpp>
#include <iostream>
#include <mongocxx/client.hpp>
#include <mongocxx/instance.hpp>
#include <mongocxx/pipeline.hpp>
#include <mongocxx/uri.hpp>

using bsoncxx::builder::basic::kvp;
using bsoncxx::builder::basic::make_array;
using bsoncxx::builder::basic::make_document;

int main() {
  mongocxx::instance inst;

  // Replace the placeholder with your Atlas connection string
  const auto uri = mongocxx::uri{"<connection-string>"};

  // Connect to your cluster
  auto client = mongocxx::client{uri};
  auto collection = client["sample_mflix"]["movies"];

  // Define the pipeline with vectorSearch query options
  mongocxx::pipeline stages;

  stages
      .append_stage(make_document(kvp(
          "$vectorSearch",
          make_document(
              kvp("index", "autoembed_index"), kvp("path", "fullplot"),
              kvp("filter",
                  make_document(kvp(
                      "$and",
                      make_array(
                          make_document(
                              kvp("year", make_document(kvp("$gt", 1980)))),
                          make_document(
                              kvp("year", make_document(kvp("$lt", 2020)))),
                          make_document(kvp(
                              "genres",
                              make_document(kvp(
                                  "$in", make_array("Action", "Adventure",
                                                    "Family"))))))))),
              kvp("query",
                  make_document(kvp(
                      "text", "epic fantasy journey with reluctant heroes"))),
              kvp("numCandidates", 100), kvp("limit", 10)))))
      .project(make_document(
          kvp("_id", 0), kvp("title", 1), kvp("fullplot", 1), kvp("year", 1),
          kvp("genres", 1),
          kvp("score", make_document(kvp("$meta", "vectorSearchScore")))));

  // Run the query and print the results
  auto cursor = collection.aggregate(stages);

  for (auto&& doc : cursor) {
    std::cout << bsoncxx::to_json(doc) << std::endl;
  }

  return 0;
}

```

#### Simple Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *time travel*. It considers up to `150` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot` and `title` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the [vector search score](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-score) for each document in the results.

```csharp
using MongoDB.Bson;
using MongoDB.Bson.Serialization.Attributes;
using MongoDB.Bson.Serialization.Conventions;
using MongoDB.Driver;

public class vectorSearchBasicQuery 
{
  // define connection to your cluster
  private const string MongoConnectionString = "<connection-string>";

  public static void Main(string[] args){
    var camelCaseConvention = new ConventionPack { new CamelCaseElementNameConvention() };
    ConventionRegistry.Register("CamelCase", camelCaseConvention, type => true);

    // connect to your cluster
    var mongoClient = new MongoClient(MongoConnectionString);

    // define namespace
    var moviesDatabase = mongoClient.GetDatabase("sample_mflix");
    var moviesCollection = moviesDatabase.GetCollection<EmbeddedMovie>("embedded_movies");

        IndexName = "vector_index",
        NumberOfCandidates = 150
    };

    // run query
    var results = moviesCollection.Aggregate()
                .VectorSearch(movie => movie.Embedding, vector, 10, options)
                .Project(Builders<EmbeddedMovie>.Projection
                  .Include(movie => movie.Title)
                  .Include(movie => movie.Plot)
                  .Exclude(movie => movie.Id)
                  .MetaVectorSearchScore(movie => movie.Score))
                .ToList();

    // print results
    foreach (var movie in results)
      {
        Console.WriteLine(movie.ToJson());
      }
  }

public class EmbeddedMovie
{
    [BsonIgnoreIfDefault]

    public string? Title { get; set; }
    public string? Plot { get; set; }
    [BsonElement("plot_embedding_voyage_3_large")]
    public double[]? Embedding { get; set; }
    public double Score { get; set; }
}

#### Filter Query

The following query filters the documents for movies released between January 01, `1955` and January 01, `1975` before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `150` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *kids adventure*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

#### ENN Example

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *world war*. It requests exact matches and limits the results to `10` documents only. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

    var options = new VectorSearchOptions<EmbeddedMovie>() {
        IndexName = "vector_index",
        Exact = true
    };

    // run query
    var results = moviesCollection.Aggregate()
                .VectorSearch(m => m.Embedding, vector, 10, options)
                .Project(Builders<EmbeddedMovie>.Projection
                  .Include(m => m.Title)
                  .Include(movie => movie.Plot))
                .ToList();

    // print results
    foreach (var movie in results)
      {
        Console.WriteLine(movie.ToJson());
      }

#### Simple Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *time travel*. It considers up to `150` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot` and `title` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the [vector search score](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-score) for each document in the results.

			{"numCandidates", 150},
			{"limit", 10},
		}}}

	projectStage := bson.D{
		{"$project", bson.D{
			{"_id", 0},
			{"plot", 1},
			{"title", 1},
			{"score", bson.D{{"$meta", "vectorSearchScore"}}},
		}}}

	cursor, err := coll.Aggregate(ctx, mongo.Pipeline{vectorSearchStage, projectStage})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("failed to retrieve data from the server: %v", err)
	}
	// Display the results
	type ProjectedMovieResult struct {
		Title string  `bson:"title"`
		Plot  string  `bson:"plot"`
		Score float64 `bson:"score"`
	}

	var results []ProjectedMovieResult
	if err = cursor.All(ctx, &results); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("failed to unmarshal retrieved docs to ProjectedMovieResult objects: %v", err)
	}
	for _, result := range results {
		fmt.Printf("Title: %v \nPlot: %v \nScore: %v \n\n", result.Title, result.Plot, result.Score)
	}
}

#### Filter Query

The following query filters the documents for movies released between January 01, `1955` and January 01, `1975` before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `150` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *kids adventure*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

MongoDB Vector Search filters the documents based on the `year` field value that ranges between 1955 and 1975. It returns documents that summarize children's adventures in the plot for movies released between 1955 and 1975.

**See also: Additional Filter Examples**

The [MongoDB Vector Search Quick Start Tutorial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/tutorials/quick-start.md#std-label-vector-search-quick-start) tutorial demonstrates other pre-filters in semantic search queries against the embedded data in the `sample_mflix.embedded_movies` collection.

#### ENN Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *world war*. It requests exact matches and limits the results to `10` documents only. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

#### Simple Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *time travel*. It considers up to `150` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot` and `title` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the [vector search score](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-score) for each document in the results.

      int limit = 10;
      int numCandidates = 150;
      
      // define pipeline 
      List<Bson> pipeline = asList(
        vectorSearch(
          fieldSearchPath,
          queryVector,
          indexName,
          limit,
          approximateVectorSearchOptions(numCandidates)),
        project(
          fields(exclude("_id"), include("title"), include("plot"),
          metaVectorSearchScore("score"))));
      
      // run query and print results
      collection.aggregate(pipeline)
        .forEach(doc -> System.out.println(doc.toJson()));	
    }

#### Filter Query

The following query filters the documents for movies released between January 01, `1955` and January 01, `1975` before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `150` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *kids adventure*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

 
            String indexName = "vector_index";  
            FieldSearchPath fieldSearchPath = fieldPath("plot_embedding_voyage_3_large");  
            long numCandidates = 150;  
            long limit = 10;  
  
            // Define filter criteria  
            Bson criteria = and(gt("year", 1955), lt("year", 1975));  
  
            // Create VectorSearchOptions  
            VectorSearchOptions options = VectorSearchOptions.approximateVectorSearchOptions(numCandidates)  
                .filter(criteria);  
  
            // Define the pipeline  
            List<Bson> pipeline = asList(  
                vectorSearch(  
                    fieldSearchPath,  
                    queryVector,  
                    indexName,  
                    limit,  
                    options  
                ),  
                project(  
                    fields(  
                        exclude("_id"),  
                        include("title"),  
                        include("plot"),  
                        include("year"),  
                        metaVectorSearchScore("score")  
                    )  
                )  
            );  
  
            // Run query and print results  
            collection.aggregate(pipeline).forEach(doc -> System.out.println(doc.toJson()));  
        }  
    }  
}

MongoDB Vector Search filters the documents based on the `year` field value that ranges between 1955 and 1975. It returns documents that summarize children's adventures in the plot for movies released between 1955 and 1975.

**See also: Additional Filter Examples**

The [MongoDB Vector Search Quick Start Tutorial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/tutorials/quick-start.md#std-label-vector-search-quick-start) tutorial demonstrates other pre-filters in semantic search queries against the embedded data in the `sample_mflix.embedded_movies` collection.

#### ENN Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *world war*. It requests exact matches and limits the results to `10` documents only. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *time travel*. It considers up to `150` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot` and `title` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the [vector search score](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-score) for each document in the results.

#### Filter Query

The following query filters the documents for movies released between January 01, `1955` and January 01, `1975` before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `150` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *kids adventure*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

          'index': 'vector_index',

                'year': {
                  '$gt': 1955
                }
              }, 
              {
                'year': {
                  '$lt': 1975
                }
              }
            ]
          },

MongoDB Vector Search filters the documents based on the `year` field value that ranges between 1955 and 1975. It returns documents that summarize children's adventures in the plot for movies released between 1955 and 1975.

**See also: Additional Filter Examples**

The [MongoDB Vector Search Quick Start Tutorial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/tutorials/quick-start.md#std-label-vector-search-quick-start) tutorial demonstrates other pre-filters in semantic search queries against the embedded data in the `sample_mflix.embedded_movies` collection.

#### Nested Field Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `reviews.comments_embedding` field in the `sample_airbnb.listingsAndReviews` collection using vector embeddings for the string *great location close to everything*. It considers up to `100` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results.

The query pre-filters the documents by matching the `address.country` field value to *United States* and number of bedrooms between 2 and 3. It then uses the `nestedOptions` option to return the document that has the *average* score from the matching child documents as the overall score for the parent document.

The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `name`, `address`, and `reviews.comments` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

Create the embeddings for the nested field and index the collection by following the instructions in [Procedure.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-create-index-procedure)

async function run() {
  try {
    await client.connect();

    // set namespace
    const database = client.db("sample_airbnb");
    const coll = database.collection("listingsAndReviews");

    // define pipeline
    const agg = [
      {
        "$vectorSearch": {
          "index": "vector_index",
          "filter": {
            "reviews.date": { "$gte": new Date("2010-01-01") }
          },
          "parentFilter": {
            "address.country": { "$in": ["United States"] },
            "bedrooms": { "$gte": 2,  "$lte": 3 }, 
            "property_type": { "$in": ["Apartment", "House"] }
          },
          "path": "reviews.comments_embedding",
          "queryVector": GREAT_LOCATION_EMBEDDING,
          "numCandidates": 100,
          "limit": 5,
          "nestedOptions": {
            "scoreMode": "avg"
          }
        }
      },
      {
        "$project": {
          "_id": 0,
          "name": 1,
          "address": 1,
          "neighborhood_overview": 1,
          "bedrooms": 1,
          "property_type": 1,
          "reviews.comments": 1,
          "score": { "$meta": "vectorSearchScore" }
        }
      }
    ];
  // run pipeline
  const result = coll.aggregate(agg);

  // print results
    await result.forEach((doc) => console.dir(JSON.stringify(doc)));
  } finally {
    await client.close();
  }
}
run().catch(console.dir);

`{"name":"Walk to beach - Cottage close to Waikiki","neighborhood_overview":"What I love about this neighborhood is that is pretty melow and quiet, but if you walk about six blocks you find all the action in waikiki and of course I love the fact that is so close to the ocean and the beautiful Kapiolani Park and you can see people exercising, kids playing in the park, etc, it's really amazing,","property_type":"House","bedrooms":3,"address":{"street":"Honolulu, HI, United States","suburb":"Diamond Head/Kapahulu/St. Louis Heights","government_area":"Primary Urban Center","market":"Oahu","country":"United States","country_code":"US","location":{"type":"Point","coordinates":[-157.81261,21.27219],"is_location_exact":false}},"reviews":[{"comments":"I went to Oahu on a girls trip with 8 of my friends for my birthday. This place met all of our wishes. There is plenty of street parking and the neighborhood feels safe enough. It's not the fanciest neighborhood, but we were very comfortable and felt like locals. The house was very clean and decorated well. The beds were comfortable, but more on the firm side, FYI. The kitchen had all the necessary tools and every appliance worked well. The bathroom was clean and the shower had strong water pressure. There is a washer and dryer that works well, but we only used it once since Marylu had left plenty of linens and towels for us. There is a large Safeway grocery store about a mile away, and a liquor store and gas station just a couple blocks down the street.\\r\\n\\r\\nMarylu was very quick to respond to my emails and was very accommodating even though we didn't need anything else or have any complaints.  \\r\\n\\r\\nWe had an amazing time and a big reason was this cottage. "},{"comments":"The cottage is lovely. It is a great place for a family or a group of friends. We were delighted to find all kind of treats in the kitchen and all needed for cooking. The sofas are comfortable and the hard wood floors beautiful. The walk to the beach is right past the zoo!"},{"comments":"The house was perfect!  We fit a group of seven comfortably when we were in town for a friend's wedding.  The well-supplied kitchen meant we could save money by preparing several meals at the house.  But the house is also close to the beach (~20 min. walk) and several good places to eat, including the delicious Side Street Inn.  \\r\\n\\r\\nI loved reading and barbecuing in the yard.  There were plenty of towels and beach supplies for everyone.  Besides the bathroom being a bit busy with seven people, it was very clean and the shower pressure and temperature level were great.  The welcome package was a nice touch.  \\r\\n\\r\\nAs others have mentioned, the only issue we had was with noise.  There's not much sound insulation between the house and the street or the neighboring houses.  I would suggest bringing earplugs if you're a light sleeper.  Also, the neighbors stopped by one night to ask that we keep the conversation down after 10 so that's good to keep in mind in advance.  \\r\\n\\r\\nAlso, a lot of the outlets are two-prong.  It could be useful to bring a 3-prong to 2-prong adapter.  \\r\\n\\r\\nWe'd all definitely stay again - thanks so much!  \\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\n"},{"comments":"The house was better than expected! Very relaxful place, with a short walk to the main strip. Wish we could have stayed there longer."},{"comments":"Great beach house and close to everything! Marylu was responsive during the whole booking process and we would absolutely book with her again. House was clean and we had a great time!"},{"comments":"My group and I were very please to stayed at Marylu's place. It honestly feels like home and Marylu makes you feel secure by responding quickly to your messages. Highly recommend this place to anybody planning on staying in waikiki."},{"comments":"The house was amazing!  Clean, spacious, and comfortable.  Marylu was very accommodating and flexible.  The yard was very nice to hang out in, and the location was excellent, much better than Waikiki.  Beautiful view of Diamond Head.  Beach supplies were even provided.  We had a large group and we all fit in comfortably, plenty of bedding, blankets and pillows.  Would highly recommend!"},{"comments":"Marylu had a great place that I would definitely recommend. Check in and check out were smooth and no hassle. Marylu was a responsive host and moved our check in time up to accomodate our arrival time. The house is in a good location with the famous Ono's right down the street and Waikiki easily within reach."},{"comments":"Marylu is kind and her response is also very quick. She is flexible for various requests. About this listing, the contents of many feedbacks are right. A positive is access to Waikiki, Diamond head, Kahala, and H1 is very nice. The cost performance is also good. A negative is road noise, but  this house is recommended for a lengthier stay and for who is not so nervous. \\r\\n"},{"comments":"The house was perfect for everything we needed. Close enough to walk to the beach and Waikiki, but far enough away to avoid all the hustle & bustle of the busy tourist area. Leonard's Malasadas, Zippy's, and Safeway are all in the neighborhood. The house is relatively close to the neighbors, and your windows will be open because of the heat so you have to be conscious to not be too loud at night. We had a little trouble getting a hold of Marylu at first, but that was due to her being out of the country. She was still able to connect with us to make sure we had the necessary check-in information. Overall, my friends and I had a great stay and I can't wait to come back!"},{"comments":"We had an absolutely great stay at Marylu's cottage. It was so 'old Hawaii'...just what we love. The place is well-equipped with tons of towels, comfy beds and a fully-stocked kitchen...perfect for the omelets I made my family every morning. The street traffic can be a little loud, but no worries since the place is so comfortable. Oh, and the mango tree outside provided the perfect sweet treat! All in all, a wonderful stay. Thanks!"},{"comments":"Host:\\r\\nMarylu made this trip easy through her ease of communication leading to the trip and during. If I had any questions Marylu would respond quickly. It is literally 8-10 mins away from everything you need; Waikiki beach, restaurants, Safeway, Starbucks and bars. We would take a cab to most of these places and the fare was always less than $10. the house has many beds. I think it can fit up to a group of 10 people. There is no A/C but the windows and ceiling fans through out made the house cooler. Marylu also provided extra towels and bed sheets which were very helpful. We were unable to get the washer machine to work and had to go to the laundry mat near by. Instructions on the machine would have helped. - Exclude the `_id` field and return only the fields stored on `mongot`.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

async function run() {
  try {
    await client.connect();

    // set namespace
    const database = client.db("sample_mflix");
    const coll = database.collection("embedded_movies");

    // define pipeline
    const agg = [
      {
        "$vectorSearch": {
          "index": "vector_index",
          "path": "plot_embedding_voyage_3_large",
          "filter": {
            "$and": [
              {
                "year": {  "$gte": 1970  }
              }, 
              {
                "year": {  "$lte": 2020 }
              },
              {  
                "genres": { "$in": ["Action", "Drama", "Comedy"] }  
              }
            ]
          },
          "queryVector": MARTIAL_ARTS_EMBEDDINGS,
          "numCandidates": 1000,
          "limit": 10,
          "returnStoredSource": true
        }
      },
      {
        "$project": {
          "_id": 0,
          "title": 1,
          "plot": 1,
          "genres": 1,
          "score": { $meta: "vectorSearchScore" }
        }
      }
    ];

    // run pipeline
  const result = coll.aggregate(agg);

  // print results
    await result.forEach((doc) => console.dir(JSON.stringify(doc)));
  } finally {
    await client.close();
  }
}
run().catch(console.dir);

#### ENN Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *world war*. It requests exact matches and limits the results to `10` documents only. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

#### Simple Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *time travel*. It considers up to `150` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot` and `title` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the [vector search score](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-score) for each document in the results.

Work with a runnable version of this example as a [Python notebook.](https://github.com/mongodb/docs-notebooks/blob/main/run-queries/ann-basic.ipynb)

#### Filter Query

The following query filters the documents for movies released between January 01, `1955` and January 01, `1975` before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `150` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *kids adventure*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

MongoDB Vector Search filters the documents based on the `year` field value that ranges between 1955 and 1975. It returns documents that summarize children's adventures in the plot for movies released between 1955 and 1975.

**See also: Additional Filter Examples**

The [MongoDB Vector Search Quick Start Tutorial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/tutorials/quick-start.md#std-label-vector-search-quick-start) tutorial demonstrates other pre-filters in semantic search queries against the embedded data in the `sample_mflix.embedded_movies` collection.

#### Nested Field Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `reviews.comments_embedding` field in the `sample_airbnb.listingsAndReviews` collection using vector embeddings for the string *great location close to everything*. It considers up to `100` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results.

The query pre-filters the documents by matching the `address.country` field value to *United States* and number of bedrooms between 2 and 3. It then uses the `nestedOptions` option to return the document that has the *average* score from the matching child documents as the overall score for the parent document.

The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `name`, `address`, and `reviews.comments` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

Create the embeddings for the nested field and index the collection by following the instructions in [Procedure.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-create-index-procedure)

The photos give a very accurate representation of the apartment. It is up 3 flights of narrow stairs in sort of dirty hallways but it wasn't a problem at all. The apartment is upstairs above a restaurant that looked nice and did a brisk business although we didn't end up eating there. The neighborhood was great - it is a residential street with cute boutiques and eateries. We walked to STOMP (had great Risotto dinner beforehand) and to 911 Memorials and to the Brooklyn Bridge and NYU - all within 1/2 hour walk. Little Italy and Chinatown are within a few blocks. Whole Foods is 3 blocks away and Dean & Deluca the opposite direction and a CVS is a block away so food and incidentals are easily taken care of. There was construction next door so that noise was present from about 8 a.m. onward but not a problem for us. Several metro lines are available within about 3-5 blocks - getting home after seeing Broadway shows was easy. Yelp gives 4.5 stars to many of the local eateries so lots of choice. We had a car and had reserved a spot at a garage on-line beforehand. Access was very easy from coming in via Holland Tunnel. \n\nWe stayed in the winter and the apartment has steam heating (which seems typical for the area) so apartment was quite warm - we had to ditch our sweaters when in the apartment. The place is very narrow and the bathroom was tiny. We were a family of 4 with 2 big teen boys and apartment worked fine for us but we didn't try to eat anything other than breakfast or snacks in the apartment - there are only 2 stools in the kitchen. We wanted to use our AppleTV but the TV is an older model without HDMI. It is large and there is cable. We appreciated that there was a closet with plenty of hangers in each bedroom as well as plenty of drawer space so we could stash our clothes away and not have to live out of a suitcase. The kitchen was well stocked with miscellaneous spices, coffee, tea and such. \n\nBrendan was very responsive to communications and happy to accommodate us with storing our bags when we arrived early before the apartment had been cleaned. We didn't need any help during out stay but definitely felt that Brendan would have been there to help us out if we needed recommendations etc. Overall we would highly recommend this apartment."}, {'comments': 'Great place, even better location. Von Spring Street aus mit der Linie 6 entweder nach Norden zur 33rd Street (nahe Empire State Building), 42nd (Grend Central), 59th (Stück östlich vom Central Park) oder mit der Linie 4 nach Süden Fulton Street raus und man ist nahe World Trade Center.\nBowery perfekt für die An- und Abreise. Die Linie J und Z verbinden diese mit der Airtrain (Linie Rot) mit dem Flughafen JFK (Fahrzeit insgesamt rund 1:30 Stunde). Eine Karte kann für beides genutzt werden.\n\nAls Alternative zum Hotel definitiv empfehlenswert. Enough privacy.\nThe bathroom was well equipped.\nThe kitchen had everything you need (no dishwasher). A little more cutlery would have been good but was quite all right.\nAs accommodation, for us as spoiled Germans, very satisfactory.\n\nThe biggest advantage, however, was the location. A small grocery store down the street (but not cheap - at 33rd Street is a Target where you can get everything you need) and the subway stations Spring Street, Lafayette or Bowery Station.\nSpring and Bowery were the most important ones from our point of view. From Spring Street, take Line 6 either north to 33rd Street (near Empire State Building), 42nd (Grend Central), 59th (east of Central Park) or Line 4 south to Fulton Street and you are close to World Trade Center.\nBowery perfect for arrival and departure. The J and Z lines connect them with the Airtrain (line red) and the JFK airport (travel time about 1:30 hours). You need a Metro Card (7 days 33 USD and a ticket for the Airtrain 5 USD) which you can buy there at the vending machine. {'name': 'Walk to beach - Cottage close to Waikiki', 'neighborhood_overview': "What I love about this neighborhood is that is pretty melow and quiet, but if you walk about six blocks you find all the action in waikiki and of course I love the fact that is so close to the ocean and the beautiful Kapiolani Park and you can see people exercising, kids playing in the park, etc, it's really amazing,", 'property_type': 'House', 'bedrooms': 3, 'address': {'street': 'Honolulu, HI, United States', 'suburb': 'Diamond Head/Kapahulu/St. Louis Heights', 'government_area': 'Primary Urban Center', 'market': 'Oahu', 'country': 'United States', 'country_code': 'US', 'location': {'type': 'Point', 'coordinates': [-157.81261, 21.27219], 'is_location_exact': False}}, 'reviews': [{'comments': "I went to Oahu on a girls trip with 8 of my friends for my birthday. We wanted to find a place that was close enough to Waikiki to party in the bars, but easy access to the highways to explore the island and not have to pay for hotel parking overnight. This place met all of our wishes. There is plenty of street parking and the neighborhood feels safe enough. It's not the fanciest neighborhood, but we were very comfortable and felt like locals. The house was very clean and decorated well. The beds were comfortable, but more on the firm side, FYI. The kitchen had all the necessary tools and every appliance worked well. The bathroom was clean and the shower had strong water pressure. There is a washer and dryer that works well, but we only used it once since Marylu had left plenty of linens and towels for us. There is a large Safeway grocery store about a mile away, and a liquor store and gas station just a couple blocks down the street.\r\n\r\nMarylu was very quick to respond to my emails and was very accommodating even though we didn't need anything else or have any complaints.  \r\n\r\nWe had an amazing time and a big reason was this cottage. If I ever visit Honolulu again, I would definitely stay here again!"}, {'comments': "Great house! It's about a 20-25 min walk to Waikiki Beach. "}, {'comments': 'The cottage is lovely. It is a great place for a family or a group of friends. We were delighted to find all kind of treats in the kitchen and all needed for cooking. Prévoir d'avoir un plus chaud que la normal à l'intérieur (en hiver en tout cas). Bien équipé et fonctionnel, bien placé... on recommande !"}], 'score': 0.6948082447052002}
```

#### Return Stored Source Query

The following query uses the `returnStoredSource` option to `true` to return only the [stored source fields](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-stored-source-definition) directly from MongoDB Vector Search, avoiding a full document lookup on the backend database. The query filters the documents for movies released between `1970` and `2020`, both inclusive, before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `1000` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *martial arts*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and return only the fields stored on `mongot`.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

#### ENN Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *world war*. It requests exact matches and limits the results to `10` documents only. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

#### Simple Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *time travel*. It considers up to `150` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot` and `title` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the [vector search score](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-score) for each document in the results.

```cpp

    mongocxx::pipeline stages;

    stages
        .append_stage(make_document(
            kvp("$vectorSearch",
                make_document(kvp("index", "vector_index"),
                              kvp("path", "plot_embedding_voyage_3_large"),
                              kvp("queryVector", vectors),
                              kvp("numCandidates", 150), kvp("limit", 10)))))
        .project(make_document(
            kvp("_id", 0), kvp("plot", 1), kvp("title", 1),
            kvp("score", make_document(kvp("$meta", "vectorSearchScore")))));

    auto cursor = collection.aggregate(stages);

    for (auto&& doc : cursor) {
      std::cout << bsoncxx::to_json(doc) << std::endl;
    }
  } catch (const std::exception& e) {
    std::cout << "Exception: " << e.what() << std::endl;
  }
  return 0;
}

#### Filter Query

The following query filters the documents for movies released between January 01, `1955` and January 01, `1975` before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `150` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *kids adventure*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

{ "plot" : "When a princess is shrunken by an evil wizard, Sinbad must undertake a quest to an island of monsters to cure her and prevent a war.", "title" : "The 7th Voyage of Sinbad", "year" : 1958, "score" : 0.71483612060546875 }

```

MongoDB Vector Search filters the documents based on the `year` field value that ranges between 1955 and 1975. It returns documents that summarize children's adventures in the plot for movies released between 1955 and 1975.

**See also: Additional Filter Examples**

The [MongoDB Vector Search Quick Start Tutorial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/tutorials/quick-start.md#std-label-vector-search-quick-start) tutorial demonstrates other pre-filters in semantic search queries against the embedded data in the `sample_mflix.embedded_movies` collection.

#### ENN Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *world war*. It requests exact matches and limits the results to `10` documents only. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

                              kvp("queryVector", vectors),
                              kvp("exact", true), kvp("limit", 10)))))
        .project(make_document(
            kvp("_id", 0), kvp("plot", 1), kvp("title", 1),
            kvp("score", make_document(kvp("$meta", "vectorSearchScore")))));

    auto cursor = collection.aggregate(stages);

    for (auto&& doc : cursor) {
      std::cout << bsoncxx::to_json(doc) << std::endl;
    }

Before you run the following examples, add the driver to your project's `Cargo.toml` file:

```toml
[dependencies]
futures = "0.3"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }

[dependencies.mongodb]
version = "3.1.0"
features = ["sync"]
```

The `futures` crate is required only for the asynchronous API, while the `sync` feature is only for the synchronous API. To learn more about the Rust driver installation, see [Download and Install](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/get-started.md#std-label-rust-quick-start-download-and-install). To learn more about the synchronous API, see [Configure the Synchronous API.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/runtimes.md#std-label-rust-runtimes-configure-sync)

#### Simple Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *time travel*. It considers up to `150` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot` and `title` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the [vector search score](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-score) for each document in the results.

#### Filter Query

The following query filters the documents for movies released between January 01, `1955` and January 01, `1975` before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `150` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *kids adventure*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

                        doc! { "year": doc! { "$lt": 1975 } }
                    ]

MongoDB Vector Search filters the documents based on the `year` field value that ranges between 1955 and 1975. It returns documents that summarize children's adventures in the plot for movies released between 1955 and 1975.

**See also: Additional Filter Examples**

The [MongoDB Vector Search Quick Start Tutorial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/tutorials/quick-start.md#std-label-vector-search-quick-start) tutorial demonstrates other pre-filters in semantic search queries against the embedded data in the `sample_mflix.embedded_movies` collection.

#### ENN Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *world war*. It requests exact matches and limits the results to `10` documents only. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

**Note:**

Pasting the `queryVector` from the sample code into your terminal might take a while depending on your machine.

#### Simple Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *time travel*. It considers up to `150` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot` and `title` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the [vector search score](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-score) for each document in the results.

1. Save the following embeddings in a file named `query-embeddings.js`:

       score: 0.7469133734703064
     }
   ]
   ```

#### Filter Query

The following query filters the documents for movies released between January 01, `1955` and January 01, `1975` before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `150` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *kids adventure*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

2. Load the file into [`mongosh`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongosh) to use the embeddings in your query:

   ```javascript
   load('/<path-to-file>/query-embeddings.js');
   ```

3. Run the query:

   ```json
   db.embedded_movies.aggregate([
     {
       "$vectorSearch": {
         "index": "vector_index",
         "path": "plot_embedding_voyage_3_large",
         "filter": {
           "$and": [
             {
               "year": {  "$gt": 1955  }
             }, 
             {
               "year": {  "$lt": 1975 }
             }
           ]
         },
         "queryVector": KIDS_ADVENTURE_EMBEDDING,
         "numCandidates": 150,
         "limit": 10
       }
     },
     {
       "$project": {
         "_id": 0,
         "title": 1,
         "plot": 1,
         "year": 1,
         "score": { $meta: "vectorSearchScore" }
       }
     }
   ])
   ```

MongoDB Vector Search filters the documents based on the `year` field value that ranges between 1955 and 1975. It returns documents that summarize children's adventures in the plot for movies released between 1955 and 1975.

**See also: Additional Filter Examples**

The [MongoDB Vector Search Quick Start Tutorial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/tutorials/quick-start.md#std-label-vector-search-quick-start) tutorial demonstrates other pre-filters in semantic search queries against the embedded data in the `sample_mflix.embedded_movies` collection.

#### Nested Field Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `reviews.comments_embedding` field in the `sample_airbnb.listingsAndReviews` collection using vector embeddings for the string *great location close to everything*. It considers up to `100` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results.

The query pre-filters the documents by matching the `address.country` field value to *United States* and number of bedrooms between 2 and 3. It then uses the `nestedOptions` option to return the document that has the *average* score from the matching child documents as the overall score for the parent document.

The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `name`, `address`, and `reviews.comments` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

Create the embeddings for the nested field and index the collection by following the instructions in [Procedure.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-create-index-procedure)

3. Run the query:

   ```json
   db.listingsAndReviews.aggregate([
     {
       "$vectorSearch": {
         "index": "vector_index",
         "filter": {
           "reviews.date": { "$gte": ISODate("2010-01-01") }
         },
         "parentFilter": {
           "address.country": { "$in": ["United States"] },
           "bedrooms": { "$gte": 2,  "$lte": 3 }, 
           "property_type": { "$in": ["Apartment", "House"] }
         },
         "path": "reviews.comments_embedding",
         "queryVector": GREAT_LOCATION_EMBEDDING,
         "numCandidates": 100,
         "limit": 5,
         "nestedOptions": {
           "scoreMode": "avg"
         }
       }
     },
     {
       "$project": {
         "_id": 0,
         "name": 1,
         "address": 1,
         "neighborhood_overview": 1,
         "bedrooms": 1,
         "property_type": 1,
         "reviews.comments": 1,
         "score": { "$meta": "vectorSearchScore" }
       }
     }
   ])
   ```

#### Return Stored Source Query

The following query uses the `returnStoredSource` option to `true` to return only the [stored source fields](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-stored-source-definition) directly from MongoDB Vector Search, avoiding a full document lookup on the backend database. The query filters the documents for movies released between `1970` and `2020`, both inclusive, before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `1000` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *martial arts*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and return only the fields stored on `mongot`.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

2. Load the file into [`mongosh`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongosh) to use the embeddings in your query.

   ```javascript
   load('/<path-to-file>/query-embeddings.js');
   ```

3. Run the query.

   ```shell
   db.embedded_movies.aggregate([
     {
       "$vectorSearch": {
         "index": "vector_index",
         "path": "plot_embedding_voyage_3_large",
         "queryVector": WORLD_WAR_EMBEDDING,
         "exact": true,
         "limit": 10
       }
     },
     {
       "$project": {
         "_id": 0,
         "plot": 1,
         "title": 1,
         "score": { $meta: "vectorSearchScore" }
       }
     }
   ])
   ```

#### Simple Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *time travel*. It considers up to `150` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot` and `title` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the [vector search score](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-score) for each document in the results.

The following query filters the documents for movies released between January 01, `1955` and January 01, `1975` before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `150` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *kids adventure*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

    // define filter
    var yearGtFilter = Builders<EmbeddedMovie>.Filter.Gt("year", 1955);
    var yearLtFilter = Builders<EmbeddedMovie>.Filter.Lt("year", 1975);
    // define options 
    var options = new VectorSearchOptions<EmbeddedMovie>() {
        Filter = Builders<EmbeddedMovie>.Filter.And(yearGtFilter, yearLtFilter),
        IndexName = "vector_index",
        NumberOfCandidates = 150
    };

    // run query
    var results = moviesCollection.Aggregate()
                .VectorSearch(m => m.Embedding, vector, 10, options)
                .Project(Builders<EmbeddedMovie>.Projection
                  .Include(m => m.Title)
                  .Include(movie => movie.Plot)
                  .Include(movie => movie.Year)
                  .MetaVectorSearchScore(m => m.Score))
                .ToList();

    // print results
    foreach (var movie in results)
      {
        Console.WriteLine(movie.ToJson());
      }
  }
}

[BsonIgnoreExtraElements]
public class EmbeddedMovie
{
    [BsonIgnoreIfDefault]
    public string Title { get; set; }
    public string Plot { get; set; }
    public int Year { get; set; }
    [BsonElement("plot_embedding_voyage_3_large")]
    public double[] Embedding { get; set; }
    public double Score { get; set; }
}

MongoDB Vector Search filters the documents based on the `year` field value that ranges between 1955 and 1975. It returns documents that summarize children's adventures in the plot for movies released between 1955 and 1975.

**See also: Additional Filter Examples**

The [MongoDB Vector Search Quick Start Tutorial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/tutorials/quick-start.md#std-label-vector-search-quick-start) tutorial demonstrates other pre-filters in semantic search queries against the embedded data in the `sample_mflix.embedded_movies` collection.

#### ENN Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *world war*. It requests exact matches and limits the results to `10` documents only. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

    var options = new VectorSearchOptions<EmbeddedMovie>() {
        IndexName = "vector_index",
        Exact = true
    };

    // run query
    var results = moviesCollection.Aggregate()
                .VectorSearch(m => m.Embedding, vector, 10, options)
                .Project(Builders<EmbeddedMovie>.Projection
                  .Include(m => m.Title)
                  .Include(movie => movie.Plot))
                .ToList();

    // print results
    foreach (var movie in results)
      {
        Console.WriteLine(movie.ToJson());
      }

}

#### Simple Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *time travel*. It considers up to `150` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot` and `title` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the [vector search score](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-score) for each document in the results.

#### Filter Query

The following query filters the documents for movies released between January 01, `1955` and January 01, `1975` before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `150` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *kids adventure*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

			{"filter", bson.D{{
				"$and", bson.A{
					bson.D{{"year", bson.D{{"$gt", 1955}}}},
					bson.D{{"year", bson.D{{"$lt", 1975}}}},
				},
			}}},
			{"queryVector", queryVector},
			{"numCandidates", 150},
			{"limit", 10},
		}}}

	projectStage := bson.D{
		{"$project", bson.D{
			{"_id", 0},
			{"plot", 1},
			{"title", 1},
			{"year", 1},
			{"score", bson.D{{"$meta", "vectorSearchScore"}}},
		}}}

	cursor, err := coll.Aggregate(ctx, mongo.Pipeline{vectorSearchStage, projectStage})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("failed to retrieve data from the server: %v", err)
	}
	// display the results
	type ProjectedMovieResult struct {
		Title string  `bson:"title"`
		Plot  string  `bson:"plot"`
		Year  int32   `bson:"year"`
		Score float64 `bson:"score"`
	}

	var results []ProjectedMovieResult
	if err = cursor.All(ctx, &results); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("failed to unmarshal retrieved docs to ProjectedMovieResult objects: %v", err)
	}
	for _, result := range results {
		fmt.Printf("Title: %v \nPlot: %v \nYear: %v \nScore: %v \n\n", result.Title, result.Plot, result.Year, result.Score)
	}
}

MongoDB Vector Search filters the documents based on the `year` field value that ranges between 1955 and 1975. It returns documents that summarize children's adventures in the plot for movies released between 1955 and 1975.

**See also: Additional Filter Examples**

The [MongoDB Vector Search Quick Start Tutorial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/tutorials/quick-start.md#std-label-vector-search-quick-start) tutorial demonstrates other pre-filters in semantic search queries against the embedded data in the `sample_mflix.embedded_movies` collection.

#### ENN Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *world war*. It requests exact matches and limits the results to `10` documents only. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

	}

#### Simple Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *time travel*. It considers up to `150` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot` and `title` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the [vector search score](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-score) for each document in the results.

      // define pipeline 
      List<Bson> pipeline = asList(

          fieldSearchPath,
          queryVector,
          indexName,
          limit,
          approximateVectorSearchOptions(numCandidates)),
        project(

          metaVectorSearchScore("score"))));

      collection.aggregate(pipeline)
        .forEach(doc -> System.out.println(doc.toJson()));

#### Filter Query

The following query filters the documents for movies released between January 01, `1955` and January 01, `1975` before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `150` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *kids adventure*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

 
            String indexName = "vector_index";  
            FieldSearchPath fieldSearchPath = fieldPath("plot_embedding_voyage_3_large");  
            long numCandidates = 150;  
            long limit = 10;  
  
            // Define filter criteria  
            Bson criteria = and(gt("year", 1955), lt("year", 1975));  
  
            // Create VectorSearchOptions  
            VectorSearchOptions options = VectorSearchOptions.approximateVectorSearchOptions(numCandidates)  
                .filter(criteria);  
  
            // Define the pipeline  
            List<Bson> pipeline = asList(  
                vectorSearch(  
                    fieldSearchPath,  
                    queryVector,  
                    indexName,  
                    limit,  
                    options  
                ),  
                project(  
                    fields(  
                        exclude("_id"),  
                        include("title"),  
                        include("plot"),  
                        include("year"),  
                        metaVectorSearchScore("score")  
                    )  
                )  
            );  
  
            // Run query and print results  
            collection.aggregate(pipeline).forEach(doc -> System.out.println(doc.toJson()));  
        }  
    }  
}

MongoDB Vector Search filters the documents based on the `year` field value that ranges between 1955 and 1975. It returns documents that summarize children's adventures in the plot for movies released between 1955 and 1975.

**See also: Additional Filter Examples**

The [MongoDB Vector Search Quick Start Tutorial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/tutorials/quick-start.md#std-label-vector-search-quick-start) tutorial demonstrates other pre-filters in semantic search queries against the embedded data in the `sample_mflix.embedded_movies` collection.

#### ENN Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *world war*. It requests exact matches and limits the results to `10` documents only. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field using vector embeddings for the string *time travel*. It considers up to `150` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `plot` and `title` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the [vector search score](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#std-label-vectorSearch-agg-pipeline-score) for each document in the results.

#### Filter Query

The following query filters the documents for movies released between January 01, `1955` and January 01, `1975` before performing the semantic search against the sample vector data. It uses the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator to perform a logical `AND` operation of the specified dates. It then searches the `plot_embedding_voyage_3_large` field in the filtered documents for `150` nearest neighbors using the vector embeddings for the string *kids adventure*, and returns `10` documents in the results. The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only `plot`, `title`, and `year` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

          'index': 'vector_index',

                'year': {
                  '$gt': 1955
                }
              }, 
              {
                'year': {
                  '$lt': 1975
                }
              }
            ]
          },

MongoDB Vector Search filters the documents based on the `year` field value that ranges between 1955 and 1975. It returns documents that summarize children's adventures in the plot for movies released between 1955 and 1975.

**See also: Additional Filter Examples**

The [MongoDB Vector Search Quick Start Tutorial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/tutorials/quick-start.md#std-label-vector-search-quick-start) tutorial demonstrates other pre-filters in semantic search queries against the embedded data in the `sample_mflix.embedded_movies` collection.

#### Nested Field Query

The following query uses the [`$vectorSearch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-vectorSearch) stage to search the `reviews.comments_embedding` field in the `sample_airbnb.listingsAndReviews` collection using vector embeddings for the string *great location close to everything*. It considers up to `100` nearest neighbors, and returns `10` documents in the results.

The query pre-filters the documents by matching the `address.country` field value to *United States* and number of bedrooms between 2 and 3. It then uses the `nestedOptions` option to return the document that has the *average* score from the matching child documents as the overall score for the parent document.

The query also specifies a [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) stage to do the following:

- Exclude the `_id` field and include only the `name`, `address`, and `reviews.comments` fields in the results.

- Add a field named `score` that shows the vector search score of the documents in the results.

Create the embeddings for the nested field and index the collection by following the instructions in [Procedure.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md#std-label-avs-create-index-procedure)
